Print and predict from a prepared calibration object

Source: R/emulator_methods.R
spDBL_calibration_input-methods.Rd

Methods for the result of calibration_prepare(). print() shows the parameter bounds, the design GP and the emulator draws. predict() calls emulator_predict(), which needs no new simulator runs, or with interval = "prediction" returns pointwise predictive distributions.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'spDBL_calibration_input'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'spDBL_calibration_input'
predict(
  object,
  newdata,
  MC = FALSE,
  interval = c("none", "prediction"),
  level = 0.95,
  ...
)

Arguments

x, object

An spDBL_calibration_input from calibration_prepare().

...

Unused.

newdata

Matrix (or vector, for one input) of mechanistic inputs.

MC

Passed to emulator_predict().

interval

"none" (the default) returns what emulator_predict() returns. "prediction" returns the pointwise predictive distribution of the field: given each emulator draw it is Gaussian, with the design-row uncertainty when calibration_prepare() propagates it; the equal-weight mixture over draws is summarised by its mean and variance, and the intervals are Gaussian with those moments.

level

Coverage of the central prediction intervals.

Value

print() returns x invisibly; predict() returns what emulator_predict() returns, or, with interval = "prediction", a list with time-indexed lists mean, sd, lower and upper of input by site matrices, plus level, distribution and n_draws.

See also

calibration_prepare(), emulator_predict()

Examples

data("dt_calibration")
d <- dt_calibration
steps <- 1:6  # the first 6 of 26 time steps, to keep the example fast
em <- emulator_learn(d$training$input, d$training$responses[steps], d$Nx, d$Ny,
  covariance = "sigma2R", episode_window = 2, nsam = 3, seed = 1)
cal <- calibration_prepare(em, d$lower, d$upper)
cal
#> spDBL calibration input: 3 emulator draws (marginal sampling), 36 sites, 6 times
#>  parameter lower upper status lengthscale
#>       eta1   2.0   4.0   free       0.674
#>       eta2   0.2   0.4   free       1.410
#>     alpha1   0.0   0.0  fixed          NA
#>     alpha2   0.0   0.2   free       0.499
#>     alpha3   0.0   0.0  fixed          NA
#> Design GP: Matern 5/2 kernel, hyperparameters per time step (6) (lengthscales on the unit scale; medians over time steps)
#> Design GP: leave-one-out RMSE 0.181, nugget 0.0001
#> Design-row GP variance is propagated within each time, independently across times 
band <- predict(cal, d$validation$input[1:2, ], interval = "prediction")
round(band$sd[[6]][, 1:4], 3)
#>       [,1]  [,2]  [,3]  [,4]
#> [1,] 0.197 0.194 0.288 0.406
#> [2,] 0.149 0.146 0.216 0.305
pred <- predict(cal, d$validation$input[1:2, ])
dim(pred[[5]])
#> [1]  2 36
